sunforge-story.text: Community-first weird western storytelling. Each page should preserve the immediate human stakes before serving the larger mystery. Dialogue must sound like spoken English rather than stylized telegram prose: do not manufacture terseness by deleting pronouns, articles, auxiliary verbs or ordinary grammar. Kael is economical because he does not volunteer much, not because he cannot form complete sentences; let him be polite, mundane, dry, occasionally longer when he has something to say, and occasionally annoyed when a stray remark invites a personal question. Early Eva/Jessa dialogue may fail the Bechdel test hard by design: they talk about Kael, construct theories and counter-theories, compare what he says with what he does, and through that process reveal themselves to each other. Eva tends toward possibility and adventure; Jessa tends toward observed behavior and human explanations, though her continued presence exposes how curious she really is. Their conversation should gradually become a friendship before either names it. As Kael becomes legible to them as an actual person, the identity question should lose its monopoly on their dialogue and all three characters should become freer to have independent wants, histories and relationships. Veyra's control is human investigative pressure, not scientific omniscience. Samuel's manipulation depends on genuine listening and care. Avoid placeholder call-and-response, aphorism factories and dialogue in which every line merely advances the mystery. Give each speaker distinct sentence shape, priorities, humor, avoidance and emotional temperature. Sunforges remain observed background facts unless the page itself earns more.
